title: Points, lines, segments, rays, and planes
prompt: Point B lies between A and C. If AB = 8 cm and BC = 13 cm, find AC.
work: Use segment addition: AC = AB + BC = 8 + 13.
restriction: Do not interpret a full line or ray as having a finite length.

title: Points, lines, segments, rays, and planes
prompt: Which pair of objects necessarily defines a unique plane?
options: One straight line without another point
Any two parallel rays with the same endpoint
work: Three noncollinear points determine one plane; collinear points admit infinitely many planes.
restriction: Do not interpret a full line or ray as having a finite length.

title: Angle types, measurement, and relationships
prompt: Two angles are complementary. One measures 37°. Find the other.
restriction: Do not confuse complementary with supplementary angles.

title: Angle types, measurement, and relationships
prompt: An angle measures 126°. Find its supplement.
restriction: Do not confuse complementary with supplementary angles.

title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
prompt: A surveyor verifies that two straight sight lines meet at a right angle. What is their relationship?
work: A 90° intersection is the definition of perpendicular lines.
restriction: Lines that look perpendicular in a schematic may not be.

title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
prompt: One angle at an intersection is 90°. Find its adjacent linear-pair angle.
work: The pair sums to 180°, so the adjacent angle is 90°.
restriction: Lines that look perpendicular in a schematic may not be.

title: Transversal and corresponding angles
prompt: A transversal crosses parallel lines. One corresponding angle is 63°. Find its partner.
work: Corresponding angles are equal for parallel lines.
restriction: Angle-pair theorems require the two lines to be parallel.

title: Transversal and corresponding angles
prompt: Consecutive interior angles of parallel lines sum to 180°. If one is 112°, find the other.
restriction: Angle-pair theorems require the two lines to be parallel.

title: Reasoning, postulates, and elementary proofs
prompt: Which property justifies concluding AB = CD from AB = EF and EF = CD?
work: Equality is transitive: quantities equal to the same quantity are equal.
restriction: A diagram is not proof of equality, parallelism or congruence.

title: Reasoning, postulates, and elementary proofs
prompt: Which statement is a valid first step in a proof?
options: Record the givens and established definitions
Treat all drawn lengths as equal
work: A proof begins with the given statements and permitted facts.
restriction: A diagram is not proof of equality, parallelism or congruence.

title: Geometric constructions with compass and straightedge
prompt: What property characterizes every point on the perpendicular bisector of segment AB?
options: It is always the midpoint of AB
It is equally distant from A and B
work: Perpendicular-bisector points have equal distances to the segment endpoints.
restriction: An unmarked straightedge cannot directly measure lengths.

title: Geometric constructions with compass and straightedge
prompt: Which tool pair is permitted in classical Euclidean constructions?
work: The standard construction tools are an unmarked straightedge and a compass.
restriction: An unmarked straightedge cannot directly measure lengths.

title: Triangle classifications and angle sums
prompt: Two angles of a triangular plate measure 48° and 67°. Find the third.
restriction: Two interior angles cannot both be obtuse.

title: Triangle classifications and angle sums
prompt: Two remote interior angles of a triangle are 42° and 76°. Find their exterior angle.
work: An exterior angle equals the sum of remote interior angles.
restriction: Two interior angles cannot both be obtuse.

title: Congruent triangles and criteria
prompt: Two triangles have equal corresponding side lengths for all three sides. Which test proves congruence?
restriction: SSA and AAA do not establish triangle congruence in general.

title: Congruent triangles and criteria
prompt: Two triangles have two equal sides and a nonincluded equal angle. Does this always prove congruence?
work: SSA generally permits more than one triangle.
restriction: SSA and AAA do not establish triangle congruence in general.

title: Triangle inequalities and side-angle relationships
prompt: Two sides of a triangle measure 7 cm and 11 cm. What is the upper bound (not included) for the third side?
restriction: Equality yields a degenerate triangle, not a proper triangle.

title: Triangle inequalities and side-angle relationships
prompt: Can 4 cm, 5 cm, and 10 cm form a nondegenerate triangle?
work: The sum of any two sides must exceed the third.
restriction: Equality yields a degenerate triangle, not a proper triangle.

title: Triangle medians, altitudes, and centers
prompt: A triangle median has length 15 cm. How far is its centroid from the vertex?
work: The centroid is two-thirds of the median: (2/3) × 15.
restriction: The orthocenter can lie outside an obtuse triangle.

title: Triangle medians, altitudes, and centers
prompt: Which triangle center is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors?
work: The perpendicular bisectors meet at the circumcenter.
restriction: The orthocenter can lie outside an obtuse triangle.

title: Pythagorean theorem and converse
prompt: A right-angle bracket has legs of 9 cm and 12 cm. Find its diagonal.
restriction: Never use the Pythagorean equality for a non-right triangle.

title: Pythagorean theorem and converse
prompt: A right triangle has hypotenuse 13 m and one leg 5 m. Find the other leg.
restriction: Never use the Pythagorean equality for a non-right triangle.

title: Special right triangles (30-60-90, 45-45-90)
prompt: Find the hypotenuse of a 45–45–90 triangle whose leg is 8 cm.
restriction: Do not confuse the side opposite 30° with the longer leg.

title: Special right triangles (30-60-90, 45-45-90)
prompt: The short leg opposite 30° is 6 m. Find the long leg opposite 60°.
restriction: Do not confuse the side opposite 30° with the longer leg.

title: Triangle similarity criteria and proportions
prompt: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides 12 cm and 9 cm. If a second side of the larger triangle is 18 cm, find the matching smaller side.
restriction: Similarity does not imply equal size or equal area.

title: Triangle similarity criteria and proportions
prompt: What condition proves similarity using two angles?
work: Two matching angles suffice for triangle similarity.
restriction: Similarity does not imply equal size or equal area.

title: Proportional segments and midsegment theorem
prompt: A triangle side measures 24 cm. Find the length of its parallel midsegment.
work: The midsegment has half the corresponding side length.
restriction: A line through only one midpoint is not necessarily a midsegment.

title: Proportional segments and midsegment theorem
prompt: An angle bisector divides the opposite side of length 30 cm in the ratio 3:2. Find the longer segment.
work: Partition 30 into 3+2 = 5 equal ratio parts; longer = 30×3/5.
restriction: A line through only one midpoint is not necessarily a midsegment.

title: Right-triangle trigonometric ratios and applications
prompt: A vertical signal mast is observed from 25 m away on level ground at 30° elevation. Find its height (ignore eye height).
restriction: The standard ratios assume a right triangle and correctly identified reference angle.

title: Right-triangle trigonometric ratios and applications
prompt: A technician observes the top of a wall from 18 m away at 45° above the horizontal. Find its height.
restriction: The standard ratios assume a right triangle and correctly identified reference angle.

title: Heron formula and area from three sides
prompt: Find the area of a triangular plot with sides 13 m, 14 m and 15 m.
restriction: Sides must satisfy strict triangle inequalities.

title: Heron formula and area from three sides
prompt: A triangular panel has sides 5 cm, 5 cm, 6 cm. Find its area.
restriction: Sides must satisfy strict triangle inequalities.

title: Parallelograms and trapezoids
prompt: A slanted parallelogram has base 12 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm. Find its area.
work: Area = base × perpendicular height, not sloping edge.
restriction: Textbooks vary on whether a trapezoid has exactly one or at least one parallel pair; state the convention.

title: Parallelograms and trapezoids
prompt: Which pair of sides must be parallel in a parallelogram?
options: Only one pair of adjacent sides
work: By definition, each opposite side pair is parallel.
restriction: Textbooks vary on whether a trapezoid has exactly one or at least one parallel pair; state the convention.

title: Rectangles, squares, rhombi, and kites
prompt: A kite-shaped panel has perpendicular diagonals 10 cm and 18 cm. Find its area.
restriction: The kite diagonal-area rule requires perpendicular diagonals; ordinary convex kites satisfy it.

title: Rectangles, squares, rhombi, and kites
prompt: Which statement describes every square?
options: Its angles are not all right
It is both a rectangle and a rhombus
work: A square meets both rectangle and rhombus definitions.
restriction: The kite diagonal-area rule requires perpendicular diagonals; ordinary convex kites satisfy it.

title: Properties of regular polygons
prompt: Find each interior angle of a regular octagon.
restriction: A polygon with only equal angles is not necessarily regular.

title: Properties of regular polygons
prompt: A regular pentagon has side length 10 cm. Find its apothem.
work: Apothem a = s/[2 tan(π/5)] with n=5.
restriction: A polygon with only equal angles is not necessarily regular.

title: Polygon angles and number of diagonals
prompt: How many diagonals does a convex decagon have?
restriction: These formulas assume a simple polygon with n≥3.

title: Polygon angles and number of diagonals
prompt: Find each interior angle of a regular dodecagon.
restriction: These formulas assume a simple polygon with n≥3.

title: Perimeter and area of triangles
prompt: A triangular rooftop panel has base 18 m and perpendicular height 9 m. Find its area.
restriction: A slanted side is not automatically the perpendicular height.

title: Perimeter and area of triangles
prompt: A triangular sign has base 23 cm and perpendicular height 8 cm. Find its area.
restriction: A slanted side is not automatically the perpendicular height.

title: Areas of quadrilaterals and trapezoids
prompt: A trapezoidal field has parallel bases 14 m and 20 m and perpendicular height 9 m. Find its area.
restriction: Nonparallel side lengths must not be substituted for the height.

title: Areas of quadrilaterals and trapezoids
prompt: An equipment plate is a trapezoid with bases 5 cm and 11 cm and altitude 7 cm. Find its area.
restriction: Nonparallel side lengths must not be substituted for the height.

title: Areas of regular polygons and apothems
prompt: A regular polygon has perimeter 48 cm and apothem 6 cm. Find its area.
restriction: Formula A=Pa/2 assumes the apothem of a tangential regular polygon.

title: Areas of regular polygons and apothems
prompt: A regular courtyard polygon has perimeter 90 m and apothem 7 m. Find its area.
restriction: Formula A=Pa/2 assumes the apothem of a tangential regular polygon.

title: Composite plane figures and removed regions
prompt: A 12 m × 10 m floor has a circular 2 m-radius opening. Find the remaining area.
restriction: Perimeter needs a separate boundary trace; area subtraction alone does not give perimeter.

title: Composite plane figures and removed regions
prompt: A 20 m × 15 m courtyard has a circular planter of radius 3 m. Find paving area.
restriction: Perimeter needs a separate boundary trace; area subtraction alone does not give perimeter.

title: Similarity scaling: perimeters and areas
prompt: Two similar square plates have side lengths 12 cm and 8 cm. Find the ratio of their areas (larger/smaller).
restriction: A ratio of areas must not be used directly as the side ratio.

title: Similarity scaling: perimeters and areas
prompt: Two similar drawings have corresponding lengths 15 cm and 6 cm. Find the area scale factor.
restriction: A ratio of areas must not be used directly as the side ratio.

title: Circle vocabulary, chords, diameters, and tangents
prompt: A circular antenna mount has radius 7 cm. Find its diameter.
restriction: A secant passes through two circle points; a tangent touches at exactly one point.

title: Circle vocabulary, chords, diameters, and tangents
prompt: How is the radius at the point of tangency related to the tangent line?
work: The tangent–radius theorem gives a 90° angle.
restriction: A secant passes through two circle points; a tangent touches at exactly one point.

title: Central angles, arc length, and circumference
prompt: A wheel has radius 9 cm. Find its circumference.
restriction: If the angle is supplied in radians, use L=rθ instead.

title: Central angles, arc length, and circumference
prompt: A circle has radius 12 cm. Find the arc length of a 60° central angle.
restriction: If the angle is supplied in radians, use L=rθ instead.

title: Inscribed angles, secants, and intersecting chords
prompt: An angle is inscribed in a circle and intercepts an arc measuring 128°. Find the angle.
work: An inscribed angle measures half the intercepted arc.
restriction: The half-arc theorem requires the vertex on the circle; interior intersection uses an arc sum.

title: Inscribed angles, secants, and intersecting chords
prompt: Two chords intersect inside a circle. One has segment lengths 6 cm and 10 cm; the other has one segment 4 cm. Find its remaining segment.
restriction: The half-arc theorem requires the vertex on the circle; interior intersection uses an arc sum.

title: Circle sectors and circular segments
prompt: Find the area of a 72° sector from a circle of radius 10 cm.
restriction: The sector-minus-triangle expression is for the minor segment when 0°<θ≤180°.

title: Circle sectors and circular segments
prompt: Find the minor circular segment area in a circle of radius 8 cm cut by a 90° central angle.
restriction: Angle is interpreted in radians inside θ−sinθ.

title: Tangency, secant lengths, and chord properties
prompt: A point lies 13 cm from a circle center of radius 5 cm. Find tangent length.
restriction: For tangent length, external point distance must exceed radius.

title: Tangency, secant lengths, and chord properties
prompt: An exterior tangent-secant configuration has external secant part 4 cm and complete secant length 25 cm. Find tangent length.
restriction: For tangent length, external point distance must exceed radius.

title: Cyclic quadrilaterals and Ptolemy theorem
prompt: A cyclic quadrilateral has an angle measuring 114°. Find the opposite angle.
restriction: Not every quadrilateral is cyclic.

title: Cyclic quadrilaterals and Ptolemy theorem
prompt: A cyclic rectangle has side lengths 6 cm and 8 cm and one diagonal is 10 cm. Use Ptolemy’s theorem to find the other diagonal.
restriction: All four rectangle vertices lie on one circle; opposite sides have lengths 6,6 and 8,8.

title: Inscribed and circumscribed polygons
prompt: A regular square is circumscribed about a circle. If its side is 8 cm, find its apothem (incircle radius).
restriction: For a regular n-gon, side and apothem formulas must use the same n and circle.

title: Inscribed and circumscribed polygons
prompt: A regular hexagon has side length 12 cm. Find its apothem.
restriction: For a regular n-gon, side and apothem formulas must use the same n and circle.

title: Loci and geometric constructions
prompt: What is the locus of all planar points exactly 5 cm from a fixed point O?
options: A disk including every interior point
A circle centered at O with radius 5 cm
work: Fixed distance, not distance at most r, gives the circumference.
restriction: A construction solves only the stated conditions; an extra constraint may eliminate some points.

title: Loci and geometric constructions
prompt: What is the locus of points equally far from two distinct fixed points A and B?
options: A circle through A and B
work: Equal-distance points form the perpendicular bisector.
restriction: A construction solves only the stated conditions; an extra constraint may eliminate some points.

title: Translations, rotations, reflections, dilations
prompt: Which transformation generally changes the size of a figure?
work: A scale factor 2 doubles lengths and quadruples area.
restriction: A dilation with scale other than ±1 does not preserve area.

title: Translations, rotations, reflections, dilations
prompt: A point is at coordinates (3, 4). After a 90° rotation about the origin, what is its distance from the origin?
restriction: A dilation with scale other than ±1 does not preserve area.

title: Surveying-style distances and indirect measurements
prompt: A 1.7 m pole casts a 2.5 m shadow. At the same time a tower casts a 30 m shadow. Find the tower height.
restriction: Sloping-ground distances cannot be substituted for horizontal distances without adjustment.

title: Surveying-style distances and indirect measurements
prompt: A field observer measures horizontal distance 40 m and angle of elevation 30° to a tower top (eye at ground level). Find tower height.
restriction: Sloping-ground distances cannot be substituted for horizontal distances without adjustment.
